source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use severe calorie restriction without medical guidance, because rapid weight loss should be the primary goal for every child above an expected growth curve.","B":"Delay changes in eating and activity habits until adolescence, because childhood routines have little influence on later weight or cardiometabolic risk.","C":"Allow unlimited recreational screen time if homework is completed, because sedentary time does not meaningfully affect healthy-weight routines in children.","D":"Build family routines around nutritious foods, water or plain milk instead of sugary drinks, regular physical activity, sleep, and reasonable screen limits."}}
source_row.rationale: Current CDC guidance supports healthy eating patterns, regular physical activity, and limits on excessive screen time, and recommends healthier beverages instead of sugar-sweetened drinks. Option D is correct. Option A promotes severe calorie restriction without medical guidance. Option B incorrectly postpones obesity-prevention habits until adolescence. Option C encourages unlimited sedentary screen time rather than a balanced activity routine.
source_row.source_detail: CDC — Tips to Support Healthy Routines for Children and Teens: support nutritious eating patterns, water/healthier beverages, regular physical activity, adequate sleep, and reasonable limits on recreational screen time as family routines.
